note: Which chart an artifact's EXTENSION sends it to. Added 2026-08-04 to close the router seam. The chart manifest (seed/CHARTS.json) said adding a chart takes 'a manifest row plus (if the behavior is new) three registered functions - no dispatch edit', and that was true for addressing and false for ROUTING: engine/router.py keyed Lean off a hardcoded `name.endswith('.lean')`, so no manifest row could ever route a file anywhere. This file is the missing half. Shape follows adapters/language_registry.py on claude/repo-intake-adapter, but it is wired into engine/router.py itself rather than into a parallel adapter path, because a second intake path is a second set of rules to keep in agreement. 2026-08-05: the default was `classify`, which meant an UNDECLARED extension was read as prose. On the real repositories that sent six .npz files — NumPy binary archives — into the English chart as ~1.9M characters of decoded garbage each, about 3,500 fabricated claims apiece. The default is now `shelf` and NO extension at all is `classify`, which is what a chat message id needs.

classes.chart: enters the named chart on the strength of its extension alone, before any content rule. `chart` must name a chart declared in seed/CHARTS.json.
classes.classify: content decides - transcript, table, or prose. This is what every non-Lean artifact did before this manifest existed.
classes.reference: READ AND COUNTED, NEVER INGESTED. A held language: the engine has no chart for it, and saying so with a count is the honest form of that. Silently walking past the file is not.
classes.shelf: skipped; hashed and counted only. This is also the default for an extension nobody declared — see the '*' row.

rules.why: the python chart: CHARTS.json row (tag `py`, behavior `python`) plus _nu_python, _classify_python and _segment_python. THIS ROW is the third thing the old contract text never mentioned.
the go chart: CHARTS.json row (tag `go`, behavior `go`) plus _nu_go, _classify_go and _segment_go.
a log has no chart of its own, but the CONTENT rules recognise log lines and pin it as a verbatim artifact. Shelving it by extension would skip that and lose the pin.
NO extension at all. A chat message id (`claude||<uuid>:3`) has no name to key on, so content decides — exactly what the router did before any manifest existed.

the DEFAULT for an extension nobody declared, written here rather than hidden in code. SHELVED, not read: an undeclared extension is far more likely to be binary than prose, and reading a NumPy archive as prose manufactures thousands of claims out of decoded noise. Declaring a new text format is a row above this one.
